facts.text: When India became independent, the princely states had the right to either merge with India or remain independent, so the Congress dream of undivided India remained incomplete.
facts.quote: These princely states had the right to either merge with India or remain independent. Therefore the Congress dream of undivided India remained incomplete.

facts.text: The Portuguese and French powers had not withdrawn their control over some parts of India.
facts.quote: The Portuguese and French powers had not withdrawn their control over some parts of India, but the country solved these problems very firmly.

facts.text: There were more than six hundred small and big princely states in India.
facts.quote: There were more than six hundred small and big princely states in India.

facts.text: Due to the influence of the non-co-operation movement, Praja Mandals were formed in the princely states; a Praja Mandal was a people's organisation working for the people of the princely states and their political rights.
facts.quote: Due to the influence of non-co-operation movement, there was beginning of political awakening among the princely states. Praja Mandals came to be formed in the princely states. Praja Mandal means people's organisation that worked for the interest of the people in the princely states and for securing political rights for them.

facts.text: In 1927 the Praja Mandals came together and formed the 'All India States People's Conference'.
facts.quote: In 1927, such Praja Mandals came together and formed an 'All India States People's Conference'.

facts.text: Home Minister Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel took the rulers of the princely states into confidence and prepared an 'Instrument of Accession' acceptable to all.
facts.quote: After the independence of India the then Home Minister Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel very diplomatically found out the way of merging the princely states in India. He took the rulers of the princely states into confidence and prepared an 'Instrument of Accession', acceptable to all.

facts.text: All the princely states merged into India except Junagad, Hyderabad and Kashmir.
facts.quote: All the princely states merged into India, except the state of Junagad, Hyderabad and Kashmir.

facts.text: Junagad was a princely state in Saurashtra; its Nawab was thinking of joining Pakistan, the people opposed him and the Nawab left for Pakistan.
facts.quote: Junagad was a princely state in Saurashtra. The people there wanted to be merged with India. But the Nawab of Junagad was thinking of joining Pakistan. The people strongly opposed his decision and the Nawab left for Pakistan.

facts.text: In February 1948 Junagad got merged into India.
facts.quote: Later in February 1948, Junagad got merged into India.

facts.text: Hyderabad was the largest princely state in India; it included Telegu, Kannada and Marathi speaking regions under the autocratic rule of the Nizam.
facts.quote: Hyderabad was the largest princely state in India. It included Telegu, Kannada and Marathi speaking regions. There was the autocratic rule of the Nizam over these provinces.

facts.text: People formed the Andhra Parishad in the Telangana region, the Maharashtra Parishad in the Marathwada region and the Karnataka Parishad in the Karnataka region.
facts.quote: the people formed organisations such as Andhra Parishad in the Telangana region, Maharashtra Parishad in the Marathwada region, Karnataka Parishad in the Karnataka region.

facts.text: In 1938 Swami Ramananda Tirth formed the Hyderabad State Congress; the Nizam banned it.
facts.quote: In 1938, Swami Ramananda Tirth formed the Hyderabad State Congress. The Nizam banned this organisation.

facts.text: The struggle was led by the militant fighter Swami Ramananda Tirth, assisted by Narayan Reddy and Siraj-ul-Hasan Tirmiji.
facts.quote: This struggle was led by a militant fighter Swami Ramananda Tirth. He was assisted by Narayan Reddy and Siraj-ul-Hasan Tirmiji.

facts.text: P.V.Narsimha Rao and Govindbhai Shroff were the faithful followers of Swamiji.
facts.quote: P.V.Narsimha Rao and Govindbhai Shroff were the faithful followers of Swamiji.

facts.text: In July 1947 the Hyderabad State Congress passed a resolution for merger of Hyderabad into India, but the Nizam took an anti-India stand.
facts.quote: In July 1947, Hyderabad State Congress passed a resolution for merger of Hyderabad state into India. The Nizam however took an anti-India stand.

facts.text: Kasim Rizvi, an associate of the Nizam, formed the organisation 'Razakar' to reject the people's demand for merger with India.
facts.quote: To reject the demand of people of Hyderabad to be merged with India, Kasim Rizvi, an associate of the Nizam, formed an organisation known as 'Razakar'.

facts.text: The Indian government started the police action against the Nizam on 13 September 1948; it was symbolically named 'Operation Polo'.
facts.quote: At last, the Indian government started the police action against the Nizam on 13 September 1948. It was symbolically named as 'Operation Polo'.

facts.text: The Nizam surrendered on 17 September 1948 and Hyderabad was merged within India.
facts.quote: Finally, the Nizam surrendered on 17 September 1948 and the state of Hyderabad was merged within India.

facts.text: There was significant contribution of the 'Arya Samaj' in the Hyderabad movement.
facts.quote: There was significant contribution of 'Arya Samaj' in this movement.

facts.text: Swami Ramananda Tirth, Govindbhai Shroff, Anant Bhalerao, Ashatai Waghmare, Manikchand Pahade etc. made a valuable contribution to the liberation of Hyderabad.
facts.quote: In this struggle Swami Ramananda Tirth, Govindbhai Shroff, Anant Bhalerao, Ashatai Waghmare, Manikchand Pahade etc. made a valuable contribution.

facts.text: Through the movement of 'Vande Mataram', students participated in the struggle for liberation of Hyderabad.
facts.quote: Through the movement of 'Vande Mataram', students participated in the struggle for liberation of Hyderabad.

facts.text: Ved Prakash, Shyamlal, Govind Pansare, Bahirji Shinde, Shridhar Vartak, Janardan Mama, Shoaib Ullah Khan etc. embraced martyrdom in the Hyderabad struggle.
facts.quote: Similarly, in this struggle Ved Prakash, Shyamlal, Govind Pansare, Bahirji Shinde, Shridhar Vartak, Janardan Mama, Shoaib Ullah Khan etc. embraced martyrdom.

facts.text: The leaders and the people in Marathwada had a lion's share in the struggle for liberation of Hyderabad.
facts.quote: Thus we can understand that the leaders and the people in Marathwada had a lion's share in the struggle for liberation of Hyderabad.

facts.text: 17 September is celebrated as 'Marathwada Mukti Din' in Marathwada.
facts.quote: 17 September is celebrated as 'Marathwada Mukti Din' in Marathwada to commemorate the struggle for liberation of Hyderabad.

facts.text: Marathwada was not included in Free India on 15 August 1947.
facts.quote: Marathwada was not included in Free India on 15 August 1947.

facts.text: After the people's struggle, Marathwada was included in independent India in 1948.
facts.quote: After the inspiring struggle of the people, this region was included in independent India in 1948.

facts.text: Hari Singh, the ruler of Kashmir, had decided to remain independent; Pakistan put pressure on him.
facts.quote: Hari Singh, the ruler of State of Kashmir, had decided to remain independent. Pakistan had intended to secure the merger of Kashmir with Pakistan. Due to this Pakistan started putting pressure on Hari Singh.

facts.text: At the instigation of Pakistan, armed intruders attacked Kashmir in October 1947; then Hari Singh signed the 'Instrument of Accession' with India.
facts.quote: At the instigation of Pakistan, armed intruders attacked Kashmir in October 1947. At that time Hari Singh signed the 'Instrument of Accession' with India.

facts.text: The Indian army won back a major portion of Kashmir, but some part remained in the possession of Pakistan.
facts.quote: The army won back a major portion of Kashmir from the possession of intruders. But some part of it remained in the possession of Pakistan.

facts.text: After independence, Chandranagar, Puduchcheri, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam were in the possession of the French.
facts.quote: Even after the independence of India, the regions of Chandranagar, Puduchcheri, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam were in the possession of the French.

facts.text: In 1949 France held a plebiscite in Chandranagar; the people voted for India and Chandranagar was handed over; later France handed over the rest.
facts.quote: In 1949 France held a plebiscite in Chandranagar. The people voted for India. Chandranagar was handed over to India. Thereafter France handed over the rest of the territories to the Government of India.

facts.text: Dr. T. B. Kunha was in the forefront of the Goa struggle and established the Goa Congress Committee.
facts.quote: In this struggle, Dr.T.B.Kunha was in the forefront. ... With the objective of building struggle against the Portuguese, he established the Goa Congress Committee.

facts.text: In 1945 Dr. Kunha founded the organisation 'Goa Youth League' in Mumbai.
facts.quote: Later in 1945, Dr. Kunha founded the organisation 'Goa Youth League' in Mumbai.

facts.text: In 1946 Dr. Kunha went to Goa, violated the ban on public speech and was sentenced to eight years of imprisonment.
facts.quote: In 1946, he went to Goa and violated the ban on public speech. For this he was sentenced to eight years of imprisonment.

facts.text: In 1946 Dr. Ram Manohar Lohiya started a Satyagraha for liberation of Goa, spoke at Madgaon despite the ban and was deported.
facts.quote: In 1946, Dr. Ram Manohar Lohiya started a Satyagraha for liberation of Goa. Violating the ban, he delivered a public speech at Madgaon in Goa. For this the Portuguese Government deported him.

facts.text: The 'Azad Gomantak Dal' was founded to liberate the Portuguese colonies of Dadra and Nagar Haveli in Gujarat.
facts.quote: During the same period, the 'Azad Gomantak Dal' was founded to liberate Portuguese colonies of Dadra and Nagar Haveli in Gujarat.

facts.text: On 2 August 1954 youths of the Azad Gomantak Dal liberated Dadra and Nagar Haveli by an armed attack.
facts.quote: On 2 August 1954, youths of Azad Gomantak Dal by making an armed attack liberated the territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli from Portuguese rule.

facts.text: Vishwanath Lavande, Rajabhau Wakankar, Sudhir Phadke, Nanasaheb Kajrekar and others took part in the attack on Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
facts.quote: Vishwanath Lavande, Rajabhau Wakankar, Sudhir Phadke, Nanasaheb Kajrekar and others took part in this attack.

facts.text: In 1954 the Goa Mukti Samiti was formed; it sent many batches of satyagrahis from Maharashtra to Goa.
facts.quote: In 1954, Goa Mukti Samiti was formed. The Samiti sent many batches of satyagrahis from Maharashtra to Goa.

facts.text: N.G.Gore, Senapati Bapat, Peter Alvares, Mahadevshastri Joshi and his wife Sudhatai and many others took part in the Goa satyagraha.
facts.quote: N.G.Gore, Senapati Bapat, Peter Alvares, Mahadevshastri Joshi and his wife Sudhatai and many others participated in the satyagraha.

facts.text: Mohan Ranade was an aggressive leader in the struggle for liberation of Goa.
facts.quote: Mohan Ranade was an aggressive leader in this struggle for liberation of Goa.

facts.text: The Portuguese did not respond to India's patient negotiations, so the Indian Government unwillingly decided to use military force.
facts.quote: The Indian Government was patiently holding negotiations with the Portuguese Government but they did not respond. At the end, the Indian Government unwillingly took the decision of using military force.

facts.text: In December 1961 the Indian Army entered Goa and the Portuguese army surrendered in a short period of time.
facts.quote: In December 1961, the Indian Army entered Goa. In a short period of time, the Portuguese army surrendered.

facts.text: On 19 December 1961 Goa was liberated from Portuguese dominion; imperialism was rooted out and India's freedom struggle was truly fulfilled.
facts.quote: On 19 December 1961, Goa was liberated from Portuguese dominion. Imperialism was completely rooted out from the Indian soil. India's freedom struggle was truly fulfilled.
